statements.text: Spam filters in email services are a common everyday use of machine learning.
statements.explanation: Most large email providers sort spam with models trained on millions of messages. You use AI every time a junk message never reaches your inbox, long before chatbots became familiar.

statements.text: A chatbot that answers in fluent sentences understands the world the way a person does.
statements.explanation: Fluent text comes from predicting likely words, not from understanding as people experience it. A model can write a confident paragraph about a place it has no way to perceive. Judge answers by checking them, not by how smooth they sound.

statements.text: Recommendation systems on streaming and shopping sites are a form of AI.
statements.explanation: Those systems learn patterns from what many people watched or bought and rank what to show you next. They are among the most widely used AI systems, even though they never talk.

statements.text: AI systems are always neutral because they are built from mathematics rather than opinions.
statements.explanation: The mathematics is neutral; the data is not. Models learn from records of human decisions and text, which carry human patterns and gaps. Bias is a known property to test for, not something math removes.

statements.text: The autocorrect and word suggestions on a phone keyboard use predictive models.
statements.explanation: Keyboard suggestions come from language models that predict the next likely word or correction from patterns in text. They are a small, fast cousin of the models behind chat assistants.

statements.text: An AI assistant learns your personal habits and remembers every conversation you have ever had with it.
statements.explanation: By default a chat assistant sees only the current conversation, plus any memory feature the product explicitly offers and shows you. Check the product's settings and privacy page to see exactly what is kept.

statements.text: Voice assistants turn speech into text with a model before they work out what you asked.
statements.explanation: Speech recognition is its own model that converts sound into words. Only after that step does another system interpret the request. Errors can enter at either stage, which is why misheard commands happen.

statements.text: If an AI answer sounds confident, that confidence is a reliable sign the answer is correct.
statements.explanation: Tone and accuracy are separate things in generated text. A model can state a wrong date or an invented source in the same calm voice it uses for a right one. Verify claims that matter through a source you trust.

statements.text: Maps apps use machine learning to estimate how long a trip will take.
statements.explanation: Travel time estimates blend live traffic with models trained on past trips along similar routes at similar times. That is why the estimate shifts as conditions change during your drive.

statements.text: AI is a single program that one company built and everyone else licenses.
statements.explanation: AI is a broad field with many methods and thousands of separate systems built by companies, universities, and open communities. Two products called AI can share almost nothing beyond the label.

statements.text: Photo apps that group pictures by the people in them are using a form of AI.
statements.explanation: Face grouping relies on models that turn each face into a pattern and match similar patterns. It is one of the earliest everyday uses of image recognition on phones and desktops.

statements.text: Once an AI system is trained, it never makes mistakes on the kind of task it was trained for.
statements.explanation: Trained models make errors, especially on inputs unlike their training data. Even strong systems have measured error rates. Treat every output as a draft to check, not a verdict.

statements.text: Search engines have used machine learning to rank results for many years.
statements.explanation: Ranking signals have been learned from data for a long time, well before conversational AI. The ranking model decides which pages appear first, which shapes what most people ever see.

statements.text: AI tools can only be used by people with a technical background.
statements.explanation: Most everyday AI hides inside ordinary products: keyboards, cameras, maps, email. Chat assistants take plain language. Skill helps you get better results, but no coding is needed to start.

statements.text: Banks use AI models to flag card transactions that look unusual.
statements.explanation: Fraud detection models compare each transaction with your usual patterns and with known fraud shapes, then flag outliers for review. A declined card on a trip is often this system at work.

statements.text: Everything an AI chatbot says is pulled word for word from a page on the internet.
statements.explanation: Chat models generate new text by predicting words from patterns learned during training. They are not quoting a stored page unless a retrieval feature supplies one. That is why they can produce sentences nobody has written before, right or wrong.

statements.text: A chat assistant can produce a plausible answer even when it has no reliable information on the topic.
statements.explanation: Generation does not stop for missing knowledge. The model fills the gap with likely-sounding text. Asking it to say when it is unsure, and checking sources, reduces the risk but does not remove it.

statements.text: AI systems have feelings and can be hurt by rude messages.
statements.explanation: Current systems produce text about feelings without having them. Politeness is still worth keeping because it shapes clearer requests and healthier habits, not because the software suffers.

statements.text: Many customer service chat windows use an AI system before a person joins the conversation.
statements.explanation: Front-line chat is often an automated assistant that handles common questions and routes the rest. Good services tell you when you are talking to software, and let you ask for a person.

statements.text: AI can read your mind through your phone's camera.
statements.explanation: Cameras capture images, and models can recognise faces, objects, or expressions in them. None of that reads thoughts. Claims of mind reading belong to fiction, not to any shipped product.

statements.text: Translation apps rely on machine learning models rather than word-by-word dictionaries.
statements.explanation: Modern translation models learn how whole sentences map between languages, which is why they handle word order and idioms far better than older dictionary lookups did. They still make mistakes with rare phrases.

statements.text: You can trust an AI summary of a document without reading the document yourself.
statements.explanation: Summaries can drop a key condition, merge two points, or invent one. For anything that matters, use the summary as a map and read the parts it points to. You can check by comparing a summary line against the source paragraph.

statements.text: The way you phrase a request to an AI assistant changes the answer you get.
statements.explanation: Wording sets the context the model predicts from. Adding who the answer is for, what format you want, and an example often turns a vague reply into a useful one. Try the same question two ways and compare.

statements.text: AI assistants are designed so they cannot produce false information.
statements.explanation: No shipped assistant is free of false output. Providers add guardrails and grounding features that reduce it, and the site's Hallucination Spotter tool exists because catching the rest is a human skill.

statements.text: A model's answers can change from one run to the next even with the same question.
statements.explanation: Most chat models sample from likely words rather than always choosing the single top one, so two runs of the same prompt can differ. That is a setting, not a malfunction, and it is why repeat checks help.

statements.text: AI will make every job disappear within a few years.
statements.explanation: Automation changes tasks inside jobs unevenly and over time; some roles shrink, others grow, and new ones appear. Sweeping deadlines are predictions, not facts. Look for evidence in your own field rather than headlines.

statements.text: Many AI features on phones run on the device itself without sending data to a server.
statements.explanation: Small models for photos, keyboards, and voice often run locally on the phone's chip. Larger tasks may go to a server. The product's privacy settings usually say which is which.

statements.text: An AI system knows when it is wrong and will always warn you.
statements.explanation: Models have no built-in sense of their own errors. Some products add confidence hints or citations, but silence is not a sign of correctness. Ask for sources and check the ones that matter.

statements.text: Asking an AI assistant to show its sources gives you something you can check.
statements.explanation: A cited source is a lead you can open and compare against the claim. Sources can still be wrong or invented, so the check is opening them, not merely seeing that they were listed.

statements.text: AI only exists inside chat apps and has no role in cars, homes, or hospitals.
statements.explanation: Driver assistance, thermostat scheduling, medical image screening, and appliance diagnostics all use machine learning. Chat is the most visible use, not the most common one.

statements.text: Content moderation on large social platforms is partly automated by AI models.
statements.explanation: Platforms use classifiers to flag likely spam, abuse, or policy breaches at a scale no human team could read. People review edge cases and appeals, which is why mistakes in both directions still happen.

statements.text: AI-generated images are always easy to spot because they look obviously fake.
statements.explanation: Generated images have become hard to tell apart from photographs at a glance. Signs like odd hands or text help sometimes, but the reliable check is provenance: where the image came from and who published it.

statements.text: Some AI tools can draft an email, a plan, or a summary from a short description.
statements.explanation: Drafting from a brief is a core strength of chat assistants. The draft is a starting point: you supply the facts, check the claims, and adjust the tone before anything goes out under your name.

statements.text: Deleting a chat in an AI app guarantees the provider has no copy of it anywhere.
statements.explanation: Deleting from your view and deleting from a provider's systems are different acts, governed by that provider's retention policy. Read the policy and the settings rather than assuming; some keep logs for a stated period.

statements.text: Live captions on video calls are produced by speech recognition models.
statements.explanation: Captioning listens to the audio and predicts the words in near real time. It is one of the most useful everyday AI features for accessibility, and it still struggles with names, accents, and crosstalk.

statements.text: Using an AI assistant to help write something is always dishonest.
statements.explanation: Assistance is a tool, like a spell checker or an editor. What matters is honesty about the process where disclosure is expected, and taking responsibility for the final text. Many workplaces and schools publish rules; follow the ones that apply to you.

statements.text: Telling an AI assistant who the audience is usually improves the answer.
statements.explanation: Audience shapes vocabulary, length, and examples. A request that names the reader, such as a new volunteer or a busy manager, gives the model a target to predict toward instead of a generic reply.

statements.text: AI models are conscious beings that have simply not admitted it yet.
statements.explanation: There is no evidence that current systems have experiences, and their designers do not claim it. Convincing talk about inner life is a product of training on human writing about inner life.

statements.text: You can improve an AI assistant's answer by pointing out what was wrong and asking again.
statements.explanation: A correction becomes part of the conversation the model predicts from, so the next answer usually reflects it. This is an everyday form of iteration, and it works best when the correction is specific.

statements.text: AI assistants can browse your private files and accounts without being given access.
statements.explanation: An assistant sees only what you paste, upload, or connect through a permission you grant. Read the permission prompts when you connect a tool, and revoke access you no longer need.
